summary: The 2023 model NEC removes the area-based outlet count. If no outlet is installed, provision for a future outlet is required.
why: The 2023 code New Jersey uses requires provision for a future island outlet if none is installed.
caveat: Verified model-edition change, not a determination for existing work. Confirm NJ amendments, rehabilitation rules, permit edition and project scope with the local official. Not a wall-countertop replacement requirement.

summary: The 2023 model NEC removes the below-counter location option for outlets serving island or peninsula surfaces.
why: The 2023 code New Jersey uses no longer allows the below-counter location for island outlets.
caveat: Verified model-edition change, not a determination for existing work. Confirm NJ amendments, rehabilitation rules, permit edition and project scope with the local official. Not a wall-countertop replacement requirement.

summary: The 2023 NEC requires GFCI protection for all kitchen receptacles. The 2020 edition required it only for receptacles serving the countertop (and those within 6 feet of a sink).
why: Back home on the 2020 code, a kitchen outlet that doesn't serve the counter, like the one behind a fridge, didn't need GFCI. New Jersey is on the 2023 code, where every kitchen outlet needs GFCI protection, so a replacement here has to be a GFCI.
caveat: Applies to kitchen receptacles that do not serve the countertop and are more than 6 feet from a sink; countertop receptacles needed GFCI under 2020 too. Replacement rule per 406.4(D)(3). Confirm NJ amendments, permit edition and scope with the local official.
